content.text:
This figure is from AC 43.13-1B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices: Aircraft Inspection and Repair, chapter 7 (aircraft hardware, control cables, and turnbuckles). Its caption: "FIGURE 7-13. Typical terminal gauge.".
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure shows a flat metal terminal gauge with several notched cutouts and two circular holes, used to check swaged cable terminals and ball fittings before and after swaging.

Labels, values, units, part numbers, and notes printed in the figure:

- 1/16 CABLE
- 3/32 SLEEVES
- BALLS
- 3/32
- 1/8
- 1/16
- MEASURE SHANK AFTER SWAGING
- MEASURE SHANK BEFORE SWAGING
- MEASURE BALL BEFORE SWAGING
- MEASURE BALL AFTER SWAGING
